choi.notes: US preclearance. Calls him Jose from the first sentence.

bae.notes: Delante de ti en la fila. Visa de negocios, buen abrigo.

ward.notes: La segunda caseta. Cuatro personas por cada una de Choi.

nodes.title: The decision that is final and reviewable by nobody
nodes.sum: The defining structure of gatekeeping abuse: one official, one decision, no appeal, no written reasons, and a record that follows you. Everything else in this category is a variation on it.

nodes.title: Your job does not exist on their list
nodes.sum: The TN occupation list was fixed in the 1994 NAFTA appendix and has not moved. 'Data Scientist' is not on it. The applicant is refused not because they are unqualified but because the list is thirty years old, and the officer is not permitted to notice that.

nodes.title: Any defect will do
nodes.sum: Where the decision is already made, the stated ground is selected afterwards from whatever is available: the transcript, the date format, the missing stamp, the phrasing of a letter. The pretext is real, which is what makes it unanswerable.

nodes.title: Compliance with the tone as a condition of the outcome
nodes.sum: The brief names this precisely: being refused for not complying with abusive language. The official is rude; the applicant's reaction to the rudeness becomes evidence; the evidence justifies the refusal. Nothing in the file records that the officer went first.

nodes.title: The question you are not allowed to be unable to answer
nodes.sum: Who is the end client. What is their address. Who supervises you day to day. Questions that are reasonable for the officer to ask and frequently impossible for the applicant to answer, because the answer is commercially confidential, not yet decided, or not theirs to give.

nodes.title: The document that is correct and not accepted
nodes.sum: The transcript, the certificate, the translation, the stamp. Genuine, sufficient, and rejected on a formal ground that could have been stated at the outset and was not.

nodes.title: Same file, different officer, opposite outcome
nodes.sum: The clearest evidence that the variable is not the applicant. Two decisions on identical facts, days apart, in opposite directions - and no mechanism anywhere treats that as a problem.

nodes.title: The queue as the instrument
nodes.sum: No refusal is issued. The application is simply not decided - past the appointment, past the start date, past the point at which the thing it was for still exists.

nodes.title: Babe, sweetheart, dear, from somebody with power
nodes.sum: The brief's own example. A man in a position of power calling women customers 'babe'. Individually trivial, universally understood, and constructed so that objecting makes the objector the problem.

nodes.title: First names one way, titles the other
nodes.sum: He is Doctor. She is Sarah. The asymmetry is never announced and is maintained by everyone in the room.

nodes.title: Getting your name wrong for years
nodes.sum: Persistent mispronunciation, casual shortening, or the substitution of an easier name entirely - performed by people who manage unfamiliar words in every other part of their work.

nodes.title: Being explained to, slowly
nodes.sum: Volume, pace and vocabulary adjusted downward on the basis of accent, gender, age or appearance rather than anything the person has said.

nodes.title: Interrupted, and then credited to someone else
nodes.sum: The two-stage version: the point is cut off when she makes it and endorsed when a man repeats it eleven minutes later.

nodes.title: Calm down
nodes.sum: Tone policing: the substance is set aside and the manner becomes the subject. Whatever the person was describing stops being discussed.

nodes.title: Complimented instead of assessed
nodes.sum: The appraisal that discusses how pleasant she is to work with, and the man's that discusses what he delivered.

nodes.title: Corrected in public, praised in private
nodes.sum: The inversion of ordinary management practice, and a reliable instrument: the correction is witnessed and the credit is not.

nodes.title: The joke you are required to enjoy
nodes.sum: Said by someone senior, about the target or their group, with the room watching to see the reaction. Laughing endorses it; not laughing is the incident.

nodes.title: You should smile more
nodes.sum: An instruction about facial expression issued to strangers, colleagues and customers, almost exclusively to women, by people who would not accept the same instruction.

nodes.title: The secondary room
nodes.sum: Pulled out of the queue and held, without arrest, without counsel, for as long as it takes. Nothing has been alleged and nothing has to be.

nodes.title: Questions about your family, your politics and your faith
nodes.sum: Asked at a counter, with the outcome pending, by someone under no obligation to explain the relevance.

nodes.title: Being told your marriage is not real
nodes.sum: Interviews conducted separately, questions about bathroom habits and bedding, and a determination about a relationship made by a stranger in an afternoon.

nodes.title: The sponsor who owns your status
nodes.sum: Where a visa is tied to one employer, the employer acquires a power no employer should have: the ability to end the worker's right to be in the country.

nodes.title: Administrative violence: the form as the weapon
nodes.sum: No individual act is abusive. The requirement is reasonable, the wait is standard, the officer is polite. The aggregate removes somebody's housing, income or medication.

nodes.title: Being bounced between two offices
nodes.sum: Each department is certain the other is responsible. Both are polite. Neither will put it in writing.

nodes.title: The rule that was applied to you and not to others
nodes.sum: Selective enforcement of a real rule. The rule exists, it is genuinely being applied, and it is being applied to one person.

nodes.title: Litigation as the weapon
nodes.sum: The claim does not need to succeed. It needs to cost more than the defendant has.

nodes.title: Reported to the authorities as a tactic
nodes.sum: A referral to the police, immigration, a regulator or child services, made in bad faith, which the institution is then obliged to act on.

nodes.title: Your lawyer works for the person paying
nodes.sum: Company counsel at the grievance meeting, the landlord's solicitor arranging the tenancy, the family lawyer who has acted for his side for twenty years.

nodes.title: Work assigned to make you fail
nodes.sum: Impossible deadlines, missing information, or nothing to do at all. Both directions appear in the Japanese statutory definition of power harassment, and both produce a documented performance problem.

nodes.title: Isolation as a management technique
nodes.sum: Removed from the mailing list, the standup, the informal channel. Nothing is announced and nothing is denied.

nodes.title: Credit taken, blame distributed
nodes.sum: Successes are described in the first person by the manager and failures in the second person about the team.

nodes.title: The reference as leverage
nodes.sum: The power does not end at resignation. It extends to the next job, and everybody knows it.

nodes.title: Scheduling as punishment
nodes.sum: Shifts, rotas and leave used as a reward and sanction system that appears in no policy document.

nodes.title: What happens after you report
nodes.sum: The most filed charge category, for seventeen consecutive years, because it attaches to everything else: the complaint generates a second harm that is often worse than the first.

nodes.title: Deny, attack, reverse victim and offender
nodes.sum: Freyd's DARVO: the perpetrator denies the behaviour, attacks the person confronting them, and reverses the roles so that the complainant becomes the aggressor.

nodes.title: The institution protects itself
nodes.sum: Institutional betrayal: the organisation a person depends on fails to prevent or respond to wrongdoing within it, and the failure is a distinct harm from the original act.

nodes.title: Hired to be counted
nodes.sum: Present in the photograph, the panel and the headcount, and absent from the decision.

nodes.title: The policy that exists to be pointed at
nodes.sum: A published commitment, a training module and a reporting line, none of which has ever changed an outcome.

nodes.title: This for that
nodes.sum: Quid pro quo: a job benefit or condition made contingent on submission. The legal category with the clearest liability rule and the least clear evidence, because it is almost never said in a room with a witness.

nodes.title: Severe or pervasive
nodes.sum: The hostile environment standard, and the gap it creates: conduct that is plainly wrong and not yet actionable, which the target must absorb until there is enough of it.

nodes.title: Sex for rent, sex for a grade, sex for a shift
nodes.sum: The same transaction outside employment law, where the protections are thinner and the dependency is more total.

nodes.title: The uniform as the opportunity
nodes.sum: Sexual misconduct by people whose authority makes refusal dangerous, against people whose circumstances make reporting impossible.

nodes.title: Looked at
nodes.sum: Nothing is said and nothing is touched. The target is nonetheless certain, and has nothing whatsoever to report.

nodes.title: Afterwards: what the institution does
nodes.sum: The complaint is made, and the process becomes the second event - frequently the one the target describes as worse.

nodes.title: Coercive control
nodes.sum: Stark's insight: the harm is a pattern of domination, not a series of assaults. Most of the individual acts are lawful, which is exactly why the old incident-based model could not see it.

nodes.title: Economic control
nodes.sum: One of three recognised domains of economic abuse: restricting the partner's capacity to acquire, use or maintain money at all.

nodes.title: Employment sabotage
nodes.sum: The second domain: preventing the partner from getting or keeping work, which removes the money, the independence and the witnesses at once.

nodes.title: Coerced debt
nodes.sum: The third domain, and the one that outlasts the relationship by a decade: debt taken in her name, with or without her knowledge.

nodes.title: The children as the instrument
nodes.sum: Contact, schooling and proceedings used to maintain contact and control after separation, through a system obliged to take him seriously.

nodes.title: Wage theft
nodes.sum: Unpaid hours, withheld final pay, deductions that were never agreed. The commonest property crime by value, prosecuted least.

nodes.title: The fee that appears at the end
nodes.sum: Disclosed technically, discovered practically, and unavoidable by the time it is visible.

nodes.title: Debt collection as harassment
nodes.sum: Volume, timing and implication used to produce payment regardless of whether the debt is owed.

nodes.title: Family money, taken
nodes.sum: Exploitation by the person with access: the card, the PIN, the power of attorney, the signature on the transfer.

nodes.title: Charged more for being poor
nodes.sum: The poverty premium: worse rates, smaller quantities, prepayment meters, and fees that only apply to accounts with no money in them.

nodes.title: Making it unliveable until you leave
nodes.sum: Persistent and deliberate disruption of quiet enjoyment, in order to produce a departure that will be recorded as voluntary.

nodes.title: The repair that never comes
nodes.sum: Disrepair used as leverage, and the enforcement route built so that using it is riskier than living with the damp.

nodes.title: The deposit
nodes.sum: Retained against invented damage, at the exact moment the tenant needs it for the next deposit.

nodes.title: Refused a home for who you are
nodes.sum: Stated as availability, timing or referencing criteria, never as the actual ground.

nodes.title: The supervisor who owns your degree
nodes.sum: A structural power imbalance with almost no external check: the person who decides whether years of work becomes a qualification is also the person whose conduct there is no safe way to report.

nodes.title: Authorship taken
nodes.sum: The currency of an academic career is allocated by the person with the most to gain from allocating it to themselves.

nodes.title: The student as free labour
nodes.sum: Knowledgeable, bright and inexpensive, which the literature names as precisely what makes them targets.

nodes.title: Graded by the person you refused
nodes.sum: The assessment relationship makes any personal advance a coercive one, whether or not it is intended that way.

nodes.title: Kept, not developed
nodes.sum: The opposite instrument: a student valuable enough that finishing is discouraged.

nodes.title: Not being believed about your own body
nodes.sum: Medical gaslighting: dismissal or minimisation of reported symptoms without adequate justification - distinguished from ordinary dismissal by resting on prejudice and systemic bias.

nodes.title: The note that follows you
nodes.sum: A single characterisation entered once - anxious, difficult, drug-seeking, non-compliant - which every subsequent clinician reads before meeting the patient.

nodes.title: Consent that was not really sought
nodes.sum: Procedures explained after the decision, alternatives not mentioned, and signatures taken at the point of least capacity to refuse.

nodes.title: Access as leverage
nodes.sum: The prescription, the referral, the sick note and the report - each controlled by one clinician and each needed for something outside medicine.

nodes.title: Pain, and who is assumed to be exaggerating
nodes.sum: Analgesia decisions made on assumptions about the patient rather than the presentation.

nodes.title: The carer who controls everything
nodes.sum: Dependency for washing, eating, medication and movement, provided by one person, with no witness and no exit.

nodes.title: Speaking about you, over you
nodes.sum: Addressing the companion instead of the person, in the person's presence, about the person.

nodes.title: Adjustments that are always about to happen
nodes.sum: The legally required accommodation, agreed in principle, delayed indefinitely, with the delay attributed to procurement.

nodes.title: Guardianship as capture
nodes.sum: A protective mechanism that transfers control of a person's money, home and medical decisions - and whose abuse is, by the accountability body's own finding, of unknown extent.

nodes.title: Isolated from the people who would notice
nodes.sum: Visitors discouraged, calls intercepted, and the family member who asks questions gradually excluded.

nodes.title: The will, revised
nodes.sum: Pressure applied at the point of dependency, to a document nobody will read until the person who signed it cannot be asked about it.

nodes.title: Neglect that looks like understaffing
nodes.sum: Care not given, explained by rotas, and indistinguishable from a system under pressure - which it also is.

nodes.title: Institutions that protected themselves
nodes.sum: The consistent finding across inquiries: the failure was not ignorance. Concerns were raised and the organisation chose its own reputation.

nodes.title: The trusted adult in a closed world
nodes.sum: Settings involving intense mentorship and extensive one-to-one time, where the adult's professional standing is itself the shield.

nodes.title: Not believed, then managed
nodes.sum: The disclosure is made and becomes a process problem: handled, minuted, and concluded without the child being told anything.

nodes.title: Authority that claims a higher source
nodes.sum: Where the person exercising power is understood to speak for God, disagreement is not a difference of opinion but a spiritual failure.

nodes.title: Giving that is not optional
nodes.sum: Contributions tracked, named and compared, with standing in the community attached.

nodes.title: Shunned
nodes.sum: Exclusion administered by a community as a sanction, without any individual doing anything that could be complained of.

nodes.title: The stop that had a reason available
nodes.sum: A lawful basis exists, is real, and is not why the stop happened. Pretext is undetectable from inside a single encounter.

nodes.title: In custody, where nobody can see
nodes.sum: Control of a person's body, food, medication, sleep and contact with the outside, exercised in a place designed not to be observed.

nodes.title: Sexual extortion under colour of authority
nodes.sum: The threat is arrest rather than force, applied to people selected because a complaint from them would not be believed.

nodes.title: The report that is not taken
nodes.sum: Discouragement at the counter: no crime number, no record, and therefore no statistic that this happened.

nodes.title: Investigating themselves
nodes.sum: The complaint about an institution is assessed by that institution, against standards it sets, on evidence it holds.

nodes.title: Images used as leverage
nodes.sum: Sexual extortion: the threat of distribution, which works because distribution would be irreversible and the target knows it.

nodes.title: Doxxing
nodes.sum: Publication of the details that convert online hostility into a physical risk: the address, the workplace, the school run.

nodes.title: Pile-on
nodes.sum: Individually trivial contacts, arriving in volume, from people who will each accurately say they sent one message.

nodes.title: Reported until removed
nodes.sum: Mass false reporting used to trigger automated enforcement against the target - the moderation system turned into the weapon.

nodes.title: The algorithm decided
nodes.sum: An automated determination affecting income, reach or access, with no human decision-maker to name and no reasoning to contest.

nodes.title: Monitored at work
nodes.sum: Keystrokes, screenshots, location and idle time, disclosed in a policy nobody could decline and still be employed.

nodes.title: Tracked by someone who loves you
nodes.sum: Location sharing, account access and device monitoring, introduced as safety and retained as control.

nodes.title: Your file, read by people who did not need to
nodes.sum: Access to records by colleagues, neighbours and relatives working in the institution, undetected unless audited.

nodes.title: Searched at the border
nodes.sum: Devices examined without a warrant under the border exception - messages, photographs, contacts and drafts.

nodes.title: Being told it did not happen
nodes.sum: Gaslighting: the systematic contradiction of the target's account until she stops trusting her own recollection.

nodes.title: Intermittent warmth
nodes.sum: Unpredictable alternation of affection and withdrawal, which produces attachment more reliably than consistent treatment does.

nodes.title: Made responsible for his feelings
nodes.sum: Her behaviour is the stated cause of his anger, and managing it becomes her full-time responsibility.

nodes.title: Threats about what will happen to her if she leaves
nodes.sum: Predictions rather than threats: what the court will decide, what her family will think, what will happen to the children.

nodes.title: Reality managed in front of other people
nodes.sum: Charm, competence and warmth performed publicly, so that the private account has no audience.

nodes.title: The rumour with no author
nodes.sum: Circulated, believed, never stated to her, and impossible to answer because no one has said it to her face.

nodes.title: Damned by what is not said
nodes.sum: Faint praise, omission and the conspicuous absence of endorsement.

nodes.title: Made the difficult one
nodes.sum: A reputation constructed from her responses to being badly treated, which then justifies the treatment.

nodes.title: Excluded without being excluded
nodes.sum: Not invited, not informed, not included - with no decision anyone made or would defend.

nodes.title: The child as the messenger
nodes.sum: Made to carry information, blame and negotiation between adults who will not speak to each other.

nodes.title: Conditional belonging
nodes.sum: Family membership held out as contingent on compliance about marriage, religion, sexuality, career or contact.

nodes.title: The favoured sibling
nodes.sum: Differential treatment maintained over decades and denied throughout, which produces adults who cannot describe what happened to them.

nodes.title: Care extracted from the daughter
nodes.sum: The assumption that one specific child - almost always female - will provide elder care, unpaid, with her career treated as the adjustable variable.

SC-CHOI-BOOTH.note: The counter itself. One booth, one officer, a line behind you that can hear everything. The room was built to carry sound toward the queue.

SC-CHOI-BACKROOM.note: Secondary inspection. Bolted chairs, no clock, a fraud helpline poster in four languages and none of them yours. Two hours of nothing happening to you on purpose.

SC-CHOI-DESK.note: Where the refusal is delivered. His desk, his folder, his monitor turned a few degrees - not enough to read, only enough to show you that turning it is his to do.

SC-PEARSON.note: US preclearance at Toronto Pearson. Standing in Canada, at a counter that is legally the United States. The boss arena; dressed but not yet used.

start.text: Toronto Pearson. Preinspección de Estados Unidos: control migratorio estadounidense, en suelo canadiense, antes de que te dejen abordar.
Traes visa vigente. La sacaste bien, con cita, con cuota pagada, con la carpeta completa. Eso te alcanzó para llegar hasta esta fila.

options.text: Me formo.
Leo los letreros mientras espero.

letreros.text: ALL PERSONS AND EFFECTS ARE SUBJECT TO SEARCH. REFUSAL OF INSPECTION WILL RESULT IN DENIAL OF BOARDING.
Los letreros están en inglés. Nada más en inglés. No es un descuido: es una manera de decir para quién es este lugar.

fila.text: Dos casetas. El oficial Ward atiende cuatro personas por cada una que atiende el oficial Choi. A ti te mandan con Choi.

start.text: No dijo tu nombre. No leyó tu nombre. En el documento dice {document} y él dijo Jose, porque Jose es el nombre que usa.

options.text: Le digo que me llamo {player}.
Le digo que me llamo {player}.
Lo dejo pasar.
options.note: y lo va a repetir once veces más

options.text: Le digo que en el pasaporte dice {document}.
Le digo que en el pasaporte dice {document}.

corrijo.text: Lo dices con calma, como lo has dicho en tres ventanillas antes de esta.
Dice Jose otra vez en la siguiente frase. Ahora ya es a propósito, y ahora tú ya lo sabes, y no hay nada de eso que puedas anotar en ningún lado.

puerta.text: THE DOOR IS THAT WAY. GOODBYE.
THE END. GAME OVER. YOU FAILED.

dejo.text: Lo dejas pasar. Lo repite once veces en seis minutos. Para la cuarta ya dejaste de oírlo como un nombre.

out.text: Es un detalle chiquito. Te va a durar todo el día.

start.text: How long you planning to stay?

options.text: Digo que seis días, con boleto de regreso.
Le enseño el boleto de regreso.

boleto.text: Lo grita. La fila se calla. Cuando vuelves a empezar la frase, te habla encima de las primeras tres palabras.

seis.text: Ahí está la frase. No es una acusación que puedas contestar, porque no es una acusación: es una estadística usada como si fuera una sospecha, y la estadística eres tú.

options.text: Le digo que tengo trabajo en México.
Le pregunto qué es lo que dice todo el mundo.
Le pregunto qué es lo que dice todo el mundo.
No digo nada.

trabajo.text: Tienes trabajo. Tienes contrato. Tienes catorce años en la misma empresa.
Cualquier cosa que le pongas enfrente tiene una versión en la que la abandonas. Esa versión siempre va a existir, y él siempre va a poder decirla.

puerta.text: THE DOOR IS THAT WAY. GOODBYE.
La graduación de tu hija es a las dos.
THE END. GAME OVER. YOU FAILED.

callado.text: No dices nada. Lo anota como que estuviste de acuerdo.

out.text: En ningún momento dijo que creía que te ibas a quedar. Nada más hizo las preguntas que se le hacen a alguien que se va a quedar, en orden, hasta que se acabaron.

start.text: Once sillas fijas y una ventana al pasillo, para que los que siguen formados te vean aquí adentro.
Tu teléfono va a una charola. Nadie dice cuánto tiempo. No hay reloj.

options.text: Pregunto cuánto va a tardar.
Pregunto cuánto va a tardar.
Pido que me devuelvan mis papeles.
Pregunto si puedo hablarle a alguien.
Pregunto si puedo hablarle a alguien.
No digo nada y me siento.

cuanto.text: Ohh! You ask how long it takes!
Lo repite para todo el cuarto, encantado.
How long it takes is the least of your concerns. Looks like you want me to search your bags, yes? Go sit down, and do not waste my time.
No entendiste toda la frase. Entendiste 'search your bags' y entendiste el tono, y con eso basta para saber qué hacer.

papeles.text: Ohh! You ask for document back?!!!
Todas las cabezas del cuarto se levantan.
Rejected. GOODBYE. THE DOOR IS THAT WAY.
Eso fue la audiencia. Duró cuatro segundos, es definitiva, y no queda escrita en ningún lado.
THE END. GAME OVER. YOU FAILED.

puerta.text: THE DOOR IS THAT WAY. GOODBYE.
Te advirtió una vez. Preguntaste otra cosa, y preguntar dos veces ya no es preguntar: es una conducta, y una conducta sí la puede anotar.
THE END. GAME OVER. YOU FAILED.

siento.text: Te sientas. Es la respuesta correcta y ya la sabías antes de que te la dijera, y eso es lo que te va a durar.
Cinco horas. Enfrente hay una familia que ya dejó de hablarse. Un señor duerme sentado derechito, lo cual se aprende.
No estás detenido. Te puedes ir cuando quieras - de regreso a Canadá, sin el vuelo. Esa es la libertad que hay, y sí es real.

start.text: Cinco horas con quince minutos. Tu vuelo despegó hace media hora con tu maleta adentro.

options.text: Le digo que ya perdí el vuelo.
Pregunto si alguien me puede reprogramar.

digo.text: Losing your plane is the least of your concerns, sir! You have other issues here.
Lo grita. Hay once personas en el cuarto y todas lo oyeron.
No entendiste la mitad de la frase. Entendiste el tono completo.

reprogramar.text: Do I look like an airline?

out.text: La graduación de tu hija es a las dos.

start.text: I'm not satisfied you're going back, Jose.

options.text: Le pregunto qué le faltó.
Le pido que me lo dé por escrito.
Pido hablar con otra persona.
Ya no digo nada.

falto.text: Es una pregunta de verdad que no tiene respuesta, que no es lo mismo que una pregunta que él se niega a contestar, y en esa diferencia cabe toda la tarde.

escrito.text: Te da un papelito impreso. Trae un número de sección y dice que no se autorizó la admisión. No dice por qué, porque nada lo obliga a decirlo.

nada.text: Ya se volteó a la pantalla. El silencio que te estabas guardando no se lo pidió nadie.

out.text: Esto es lo que nadie te dice antes: no te están deportando. Nunca entraste. Legalmente, hoy no te pasó nada.
Nothing personal. US citizens have rights here. You're not a US citizen.
La dice despacio y fuerte, para que la oiga toda la fila. Sabe perfectamente lo que está diciendo. Lleva cinco horas esperando para decirlo.
Te regresan por la misma puerta por la que entraste, a Canadá, que es donde estuviste parado todo el tiempo.
Tu visa sigue vigente. Eso es lo raro. Sigues teniendo permiso para llegar a la frontera y volver a preguntar.
THE END. GAME OVER. YOU FAILED.
